summary: A small CCC-built open-air shelter above the Snake River in Yellowstone, used only briefly before its trail was abandoned decades ago.

facts.design: 8x8 ft open-air wood-frame cab, built by the CCC as a secondary lookout

access.note: Access trail to the lookout was abandoned decades ago; no current maintenance or public-access program is documented.

visit.trail_note: No maintained trail; the historic approach was abandoned decades ago.

facts.agency: National Park Service - Yellowstone National Park

events.note: Structural members may have been completed in 1934, but the building was not erected until 1935 by the CCC
NHLR: 'Most probably no longer used some time in the mid to late 1940's'; exact year unknown, and the access trail was abandoned decades ago
Nominated by Ed Stark; registered February 28, 2021

evidence.supports: 2 mi east of South Entrance / elevation
evidence.quote: 2 miles east of South Entrance to Yellowstone NP

evidence.supports: only remaining open-air structure, built by CCC as secondary lookout
evidence.quote: The 8x8 wood frame building is the only remaining open air structure built in Yellowstone National Park, constructed as a secondary lookout by the CCC.
The structural members may have been completed in 1934, However the building wasn’t erected until 1935 by the CCC and probably not used until 1936.
Building #699, Yellowstone National Park, Teton County, Wyoming .

evidence.supports: abandoned mid-to-late 1940s, trail abandoned decades ago
evidence.quote: Most probably no longer used some time in the mid to late 1940’s and the trail to the lookout was abandoned decades ago.

evidence.supports: nominated by Ed Stark, registered Feb 28 2021
FFLA classes it as a shelter / non-lookout structure, standing

corrections.why: NHLR describes it as an 8x8 open-air structure, not a classic tower, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association's own Wyoming roster files Snake River under 'lookout sites / non-lookout structures' and labels its type 'Shelter', not a tower.

notes_for_editor: No new photos found beyond those already on the tower record. The exact abandonment year is unknown (NHLR hedges with 'most probably ... mid to late 1940's'); I used 1945 as a placeholder year for the 'abandoned' event rather than inventing precision. The kind correction (tower -> shelter) is worth a human look since 'tower' vs 'shelter' is partly a classification judgment, not a hard fact.
